exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: Here is how a strong engineer explains a different project — a garden club supply plan — so you can copy the moves, not the numbers.

traits.sample: I used the greatest common factor of 20 trowels and 28 seed packets to build 4 identical garden kits with nothing left over.
traits.why: Saying GCF and what it guarantees hits the 'both correct with explanation' level of the rubric.

traits.sample: The sprinklers run every 6 days and 8 days, so they overlap every 24 days because 24 is the least common multiple.
traits.why: Explaining why LCM answers the timing question shows real understanding, not a lucky number.

traits.sample: My divisor was 4 kits, and the quotient told me each kit gets exactly 5 trowels and 7 seed packets.
traits.why: Words like divisor and quotient show the writer knows what each number means.

traits.trait: Connects math to the budget decision
traits.sample: The total was $96.40, so each kit costs $24.10. That stays under our $25-per-kit limit, so the plan works.
traits.why: Tying decimal division back to the budget rule shows the math drove the decision.
